How to generate a RESTful API request on Cisco Nexus Dashboard?
Version: 6.3.1
API name: get information of device connector versions

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends an HTTP GET request to retrieve Device Connector Versions information from a specified URL. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. The URL points to a JSON file containing Device Connector Versions information.

params.description: Optional query parameters to include in the GET request as key-value pairs.

message.content:
Below is a step‑by‑step guide on how to generate a **RESTful API request** for the **“Get information of device connector versions”** API in **Cisco Nexus Dashboard 6.3.1**. I’ve broken it down into three parts: 1. **Finding the API endpoint & required parameters** 2. **Using the Cisco Nexus Dashboard UI to generate the request** 3. **Exporting / testing the request (cURL / Python)** --- ## 1. Locate the API Endpoint & Parameters | Item | Details | |------|---------| | **API Name** | Get information of device connector versions | | **HTTP Method** | `GET` | | **Base URL** | `https:///api/v1` (replace `` with your actual host) | | **Endpoint Path** | `/device-connector/versions` | | **Full URL** | `https:///api/v1/device-connector/versions` | | **Query Parameters** | *None* (this endpoint typically returns all available connector versions) | | **Headers** | `Authorization: Bearer `
`Accept: application/json` | > **Tip:** > If you’re unsure about the exact path, you can use the **API Explorer** in the Dashboard (see step 2) – it will list all available endpoints and their details. --- ## 2. Generate the Request in Cisco Nexus Dashboard 1. **Log in** to your Cisco Nexus Dashboard. 2. In the left‑hand navigation pane, click on **“Developer”** → **“API Explorer”**. 3. In the **API Explorer** panel: - **Search** for “device connector” or “connector versions”. - Click on the **“Get information of device connector versions”** entry. 4. The right side will display the **API details**: - **Method** (`GET`) - **Endpoint** (`/device-connector/versions`) - **Parameters** (none for this call) - **Headers** (you’ll need to supply an Authorization token). 5. Click the **“Generate Request”** button. - The Dashboard will automatically create a **sample request** in the **Request Builder** pane. - You’ll see the **full URL**, **headers**, and a **preview of the response** (if you already have a valid token). 6. **Copy** the generated request. - The Dashboard provides a **“Copy to Clipboard”** button next to the request. - You can also click **“Show Raw”** to view the raw cURL command. --- ## 3. Export / Test the Request ### a. Using cURL (Command Line) ```bash curl -X GET \ https:///api/v1/device-connector/versions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer " \ -H "Accept: application/json" ``` Replace `` and `` with your actual values. ### b. Using Python (Requests Library) ```python import requests url = "https:///api/v1/device-connector/versions" headers = { "Authorization": "Bearer ", "Accept": "application/json", } response = requests.get(url, headers=headers) print(response.status_code) print(response.json()) ``` ### c. Using Postman 1. Open **Postman**. 2. Create a new **GET** request. 3. Paste the full URL (`https:///api/v1/device-connector/versions`). 4. Under **Headers**, add: - `Authorization: Bearer ` - `Accept: application/json` 5. Hit **Send** and inspect the response. --- ## Optional: Use the Tool to Fetch Data (Python) If you already have the URL and want to fetch the data programmatically using the provided tool, you can do so like this: ```json { "url": "https:///api/v1/device-connector/versions", "params": {} } ``` > **Note:** > The tool requires a valid URL. If you don’t have one yet, follow the steps above to generate it. --- ### Quick Checklist - [ ] Replace `` with your actual host. - [ ] Replace `` with a valid bearer token. - [ ] Verify that the endpoint `/device-connector/versions` is correct in your environment. - [ ] Test the request using cURL / Python / Postman. Feel free to let me know if you hit any snags or need help generating the access token!
